Factor and Optima

Story

A father, a son, and a lesson about connection.

5 min read

Once upon a time there lived Factor. Fate had not chosen him; more than that, it had punished him in some way. For this Factor grew angry at Fate and decided to defeat it and restore justice. With enormous effort Fate was defeated, and Factor got what was his. Yet, for all that, he did not become happy.

Factor wanted to get angry at God, so that he could win his happiness by force. But every time he almost managed to get angry, God gave him a small gift that made Factor happy, and so he simply could not be angry at Him. After several failed attempts to get angry, the man began to ask God: "Why are you good to me, and why won't you let me fall into anger?"

One day, during yet another failed attempt to get angry, Factor asked the question again: "Why won't you let me fall into anger?" And suddenly Factor understood why: because God gives goodness. That is God's mission, and He will do it forever.

God helped Factor get what he had wanted so much. He decided to marry a beautiful and wise woman named Sophia. They had a son and named him Optima. Factor built up a vast estate and had plenty of food, money and wisdom. Everything he had ever wished for, he received in abundance, as soon as he decided that he wanted it.

Optima became a builder who loved to build enormous castles of sand. These structures were so grand and so beautiful that cities and hotels paid him to build them.

Once he was invited to Oceania. There were beautiful beaches there and a resort atmosphere. Optima's art would fit perfectly into the look of the resort hotel that had invited him.

When he arrived, he set to work. Optima decided to build over the whole stretch of the coast that had been given to him. He worked carefully through every detail and every street. He knew that the waves could wash away all his work, and for that case Optima had glue. The glue let the sand hold together much longer, even after the waves.

One day some teenagers came to the beach. They were mischievous and rebellious. Unfortunately, they broke a large part of the city, because it was so beautiful that it simply begged to be broken. Their parents paid the fines, but part of the city was destroyed all the same.

Irritated by all this, Optima put up a fence around the site. He restored the ruined parts, but no longer with delight, as before, only because it had to be done. He was a little angry, but he kept himself in hand.

One day, while the work on the city was still going on, a storm struck the island and destroyed the city once again, a bigger part of it this time, along with the fences. Optima fell into anger: "Why can't I ever finish this sandcastle?! Can I have some normal weather, please?!"

He began building the castle again and decided to do it all in one go. In a fever, the builder built beautiful streets, noble houses, majestic avenues. He reached the shore and realised that he had forgotten to add glue to the sand to make it harder.

Optima grew even angrier, now at himself as well. A light storm began, but he did not give up. Every time some of the houses were washed away, he built new ones, without a plan now, but with glue. Yet the glue had no time to dry. Optima kept on restoring the city every time the storm washed it away. The weather kept getting worse. It came to the point that he dug an enormous moat and lined it with wood to keep the waves from reaching the city. Optima became more and more manic, and the storm stronger and stronger.

It was night, with a downpour and a storm. It was the worst weather of his whole stay on the island. Optima cursed everything: his work, those teenagers, and the weather. He even fought against imaginary gods of the sea and the sky, who had set themselves against him. He had completely lost his mind.

There was a small earthquake. The builder, focused on his work, had already declared war on the gods of the earth. Then silence fell. The rain had stopped, and the water had drawn back from the shore. A minute of calm, and exactly the kind and manner of building he had had at the beginning. Optima was already laughing at Poseidon and the other ancient gods. He laughed at Fate, and at God. He thought he had outwitted them and won.

The water had never drawn back this far before. The builder began to be afraid, because he knew this could be the sign of a tsunami. He raised his head and saw an enormous wave coming.

It swept him away. Even during the tsunami he fought and struggled for his life, so that he could carry on with his work.

He woke up on that same beach, clean now. The sun was shining, everything was beautiful. The wave had been small enough that he did not drown, and all around, things were only a little damaged. Optima calmed down and looked at the weather forecast. He had become something greater than just a person who reproduces drawings with his hands. He began to build his structures with the outside world: with the weather, with agreements and with feelings.
